title: Polyglot fanout + hedging adapter for OpenAI Chat Completions mapping
creator: Ava Patel
description: Background: We need a robust compatibility layer that maps incoming OpenAI Chat Completions (OA-CC) requests into Redwood's internal request model, and maps responses (including streaming deltas, function/tool call signals, and structured output tokens) back to OA-compatible responses. This ticket implements a polyglot adapter that can: (1) fan out a single OA request to multiple Redwood model variants for hedged latency/cost; (2) canonicalize differences in OA payload shapes and fields into our internal proto; (3) preserve streaming semantics and patch responses back into a single OA-style stream; (4) surface tool/function call intents from Redwood structured output and ensure OA function call fields are populated deterministically. The adapter must be resilient to mismatched model behaviors (e.g., some variants emitting function_call early, others later), support prefix/KV cache reuse, and maintain auditable mapping for observability and billing. This is critical for the hosted OA-compat offering and for customers who rely on OA chat semantics.
acceptance_criteria: Adapter accepts OA-CC v1 request payloads and produces equivalent Redwood internal requests for streaming and non-streaming modes
Fanout mode: single OA request can be dispatched to multiple model variants; responses are merged into one OA-compatible stream preserving event ordering and token-level deltas
Hedging policy: implement latency vs cost hedging with configurable thresholds; adapter chooses winner and gracefully cancels losers while emitting consistent OA response events

Function/tool calls: function_call objects and tool invocation signals from any variant are normalized to OA function_call output shape; multi-variant conflicts resolved deterministically with configurable tie-breaker (priority list or majority-vote)
Structured output: JSON/structured responses validated against provided shape/schema; when validation fails, adapter emits OA-style assistant content plus a structured-validation warning field
Edge cases: backpressure and partial responses handled without duplication; reconnect/resume semantics work for streaming clients (HTTP chunked + SSE) per spec
Observability: every mapped request/response pair includes mapping metadata in trace/span and a mapping summary visible in Console (route-level), and cost attribution is preserved
Automated tests cover: single-variant mapping, fanout merging, hedging winner selection, function_call normalization, and structured-output validation failures

2025-02-12 - Diego Ramos: Spike completed. Prototype can map choices[ ] -> delta events and rehydrate into OA stream. Caveat: current delta merging uses naive interleaving; needs deterministic token ordering for reproducibility.
2025-02-18 - Diego Ramos: Implemented basic fanout dispatch and winner selection by latency threshold. Pushed experimental branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/2103
2025-02-20 - PM review (Lina Chen): Confirmed acceptance criteria for function_call tie-breaker should default to model priority list, with an opt-in "majority_vote" mode for customers. Added to AC.
2025-02-24 - Security (Jamal Ortiz): Flagged KMS usage for per-request mapping metadata; recommended we avoid embedding customer secrets in span attributes. Not blocking.

2025-02-26 - Diego Ramos: Added structured-output validation step using existing eval schema registry. On validation failure adapter appends a structured_output_error event and includes sanitized example tokens in the stream.

2025-02-27 - QA (Marta Liu): Started end-to-end tests using mock OA clients. Found a bug where partial function_call.name emitted by one variant and full signature by another caused duplicate function_call events. Patch in PR 2103 fixes de-duplication logic.
